title: I built a free action roguelite with AI-assisted coding and player feedback — CHAIN / SHIFT
author: PencilTideStudio
selftext:
Hey everyone!

I've been developing CHAIN / SHIFT, a free browser-based action roguelite, using AI-assisted coding and a lot of iteration based on playtesting.

The main mechanic is changing enemy colors with a dash, then triggering chain reactions to destroy entire groups.

One thing I've learned is that getting a game running with AI assistance is much easier than making it genuinely fun and balanced.

During development, I ran into several issues:

* Bosses had too much HP, and some weapons felt almost useless against them.
* Screen shake and visual effects sometimes made combat hard to read.
* An English-speaking playtester had trouble understanding upgrades and using the controls with a touchpad.
* Different characters initially felt too similar because they shared the same weapon evolution choices.

I used AI to help implement and revise the game code, then tested the changes and adjusted the design based on what worked and what didn't.

One specific example was a bug in my relay-defense map. The overload timer could keep advancing even while the relay was on cooldown, causing unfair enemy reinforcements. I used AI-assisted coding to investigate and revise the game logic, then tested the updated behavior.

This taught me that AI-generated code still needs careful testing, especially when different gameplay systems interact.

The game now has three playable pilots with different weapon paths, three maps with unique mechanics, and persistent unlocks.

The attached video shows actual gameplay recorded from the game.

I'm still learning how to balance challenging combat with accessibility, especially in a game with lots of enemies and chain reactions.

For other developers using AI-assisted coding, how do you approach playtesting and balancing systems that become increasingly complex?

You can try the current free browser version here:

[https://penciltide.itch.io/chain-shift](https://penciltide.itch.io/chain-shift)
